THE HEALTH OF ALTRINCHAM, IN the quarter yid& has just expired there were evident signs that the outbreak of smallpox wa, declining in Atrineham sub- district. The first quarters report of this year had 9 deaths, then in the June period the total rose to 28, and in the three months following they declined to 14. Here then we have had a total of 51 deaths from this disease during the first 9 months of this year. This is a great sacrifice of life to this disease, and now that it is on the decline no efforts should be spared if, isolating all freak casee and stamping out the disease. In our report on the March quarter we then pointed out the 9 deaths from smallpox, and we certainly think that if strenuous exer- tions had then been made to check the disease, many of the deaths recorded would not have taken place. funk a fatality from this one disease is deplorable, and it must be both painful and humiliating to the inhabi- tants to see so many victims falling to this
scourge. the marriages in Altrincham during the June qualter a this year numbered 78, and these were below the total that took place in the same period of last year by 13.

In the September quarter there were 27 births in the sub-Mstrict of Altrincham, which Mao includes bale and Bowdon. lu the same three months ot last year there were 257 births or 30 more than the present total. She average of the corresponding periods of 1074.5-6 lead us to expect 114 deaths, but there, were 122, showing no excess of 8. Ihie is, however, a far better return than the one for the same quarter, fur there were then 153 deaths, or 31 more than the present total. Scarlet fever WAS not fatal in Altrincham, as there was only one death due to it against 3 in June. Fever was not credited with one death. yl the 122 deaths, as many as 27 were those Cl infants under 1 year, and 33 deaths were those of persons who had attained the age of 60 years and upwards. there were 4 • deaths trom violence, inquests were held on 8 bodies, and B.died in the two hospitals ot Altrincham. Wtimalow, Northenden, and Mobberley had BO births, Lull as the deaths were 28 they were I below the average for the quarter. Thie ia a great improvement on the June return, tor then were were 48 deaths, or 20 more than the present total. Nine of the 28 deaths in these places re- ferred to persons who had attained 60 years and upwards. Lyinm, Yartington, High Legh, and Aston contribute a light bill of mortality. There were only '29 deaths, and theee were below the number expected by 7. in the June quarter there anus a return of 44 • deaths, or 15 more than what took place in the period just ended. Where was 1 death due to scarlet fever, and ato violence. Who births numbered 58. Knutstord, Mere, and linstherne had 61 birdie, and the deaths being 34, they were under the average for the quarter by 4. The June return gave 44 deaths, or 10 more than what occurred in the last quarter. Unfor- tunately smallpox made its appearance, and carried oil 2. It is to hoped that the people in Knutsford sub-district, unlike those of Adaincham, will take such measures as to prevent the disease from assuming such pro- portions as it did in Altrincham. Scarlet fever was fatal in 2 cases. Bight deaths took place in the workhouse of Knuteford.
lIIE CRISIS IN FRANCE. IRE BUDGET DEFERRED.

The inquiry into the manner in which the Government had acted during the late elections has been reeisted in the Senate by the Minister, the Duo de Broglie, who de- clared that the inquiry proposed by the Chamber woe illegal. Nothing is known as to the Eucceseors of M. de Broglie and his colleagno. It ie feared that the Senate will consent to a nomad die3ollltioll. In that cur,, says a Daily Falce correspondent, "the Chamber trot hod this dissolution illegal , and attempt to meet. Then the Marshal , will see hie opportunity to bring bayonets on the stage and forcibly dieperso them. What is to come after no man can predict with any certainty ; but my belief is the country will rise in irresistible force and sweep away the wrong.doer—not, however, perhope, without much bloodshed." Tuesday'e journal Official announced that the .Frencli Monateri had given in their resignations to Marshal MacHation, awl that , he had accepted them. The Ministers will I only retain Utile until their successors have I ' been appointed. , In the °clamber on Tuesday it was re. solved, in consequence of the viewe expressed the previous day in the Ornate by the Duo I , de Broglie, to postpone the debate upon the ' 1 validity of the election of Baron Bailie, , .
